title: Jev questions
description: A set of named Jev questions in TypeSafe's request shape. Each name becomes a key in the answers object, so pick names your code can read, like is_urgent or frustration.

questions.title: Questions
questions.description: One entry per question. The name is the key Jev answers under; the value is what you ask.

oneOf.title: Yes / No
oneOf.description: Jev answers with a probability between 0 and 1 that the answer is yes.

instructions.title: Question
instructions.description: Ask it as a yes / no question. Jev reads the state you pass alongside it.

criteria.title: What counts
criteria.description: Optional. Spell out what a yes and a no look like when the question alone could be read two ways.

true.title: Means yes
true.description: Describe the situation that should count as yes.

false.title: Means no
false.description: Describe the situation that should count as no.

oneOf.title: Score
oneOf.description: Jev answers with an expected score on the rubric: 0 is the first line, 1 the second, and so on. It can land between levels, so 1.5 means between the second and third line.

instructions.title: Question
instructions.description: What is being rated. The rubric below defines the scale.

criteria.title: Rubric, lowest first
criteria.description: One line per level, lowest first. The first line is level 0, the second is level 1. At least two lines.

items.title: Level
items.description: What this level looks like, in a sentence.

oneOf.title: Choice
oneOf.description: Jev picks exactly one of the labels and answers with its name.

instructions.title: Question
instructions.description: What to classify. The labels below are the only possible answers.

criteria.title: Labels
criteria.description: The label is the name Jev answers with; the text tells Jev when to pick it. At least two labels.

additionalProperties.title: When to pick it
additionalProperties.description: Describe the case this label covers.
